observations.content: User provided context-only implementation reference packets (preparation turns 1–9/12) for an observational-memory pi extension; no implementation was requested in those historical packets.

Historical task requirement: expose actual pi usage cost of every observer and consolidator worker run to the parent orchestrator, including ephemeral and unsuccessful runs whenever valid usage exists; persist valid costs as session-ledger entries keyed by role/run identity; aggregate all branch costs including abandoned branches while ignoring missing, malformed, non-finite, or negative costs; surface totals in status/footer and add focused tests for aggregation, invalid entries, handoff, and display.

The observational-memory extension plan defines a default-OFF per-session /om gate persisted through om.enabled ledger entries; when off, the extension should be inert and invisible. It uses parallel observer subprocesses and a single consolidator subprocess, branch-local observation ledger entries, deterministic compaction, TUI status, and durable project .memory topic files plus JOURNEY.md.

Historical plan decisions: phased short-term tier then long-term tier; workers are ordinary recorded global pi sessions launched via child_process.spawn, not subagents; OM modules are vendored and trimmed; one env-parameterized worker extension supports observer/consolidator; orchestrator assigns unique timestamp IDs; dev model is claude-sonnet-4-6; initial gate defaults OFF.

Plan specifies observation records with timestamp/content/tokenCount and om.observations.recorded / om.observations.dropped ledger entries, coverage watermarks, branch-aware folding, deterministic compact rendering, /tree rollback for buffer, and oldest-first consolidation. Consolidator edits scoped .memory files and the orchestrator tombstones its handed batch intersected with still-active observations on clean exit.

The historical reference describes .memory/JOURNEY.md as a consolidator-maintained descriptive project arc, appended in dated segments, compressing only old segments after journeyTargetTokens; it is excluded from topic maps and pushed verbatim as the first compaction section.

Reference README reports Phase A and B implemented, with commands /om, /om on/off, /om:status, /om:compact, and /om:consolidate; worker sessions are recorded globally and transient handoff files reside in .memory/.runs.

Reference config defaults in src/config.ts differ from the earlier plan: chunkTokens 10000, poolTargetTokens 10000, consolidateAtPoolTokens 15000, compactAtContextTokens 100000, tailTokens 20000, journeyTargetTokens 1000, observerConcurrency 4, with Sonnet 4.6 observer low and consolidator medium; resumeAfterMidRunCompaction defaults true.

Reference src/hooks/observer-trigger.ts launches parallel fixed-boundary observer chunks, serializes inert transcript data into the recorded pi -p prompt, validates the result file, assigns collision-free timestamp IDs and token counts in code, then commits observations and updates UI.

Reference src/hooks/compaction-hook.ts snaps compaction cutoff to valid observation chunk boundaries, uses canSkipObserverWait when in-flight observers cannot affect the projection, waits otherwise, then renders journey, memory map, and active observations.

Reference src/hooks/compaction-trigger.ts triggers compaction at context threshold on turn_end, ignores retryable provider/network errors, and optionally resumes a mid-run compaction with hidden om.resume custom input; terminal turns are not resumed.

Reference UI uses a footer with observer/pool/context gauges, a combined om-workers widget for parallel workers, and status output including worker counts, buffer/pool, compaction wait, topic count, journey size, context, last error, and a timeline.

The provided historical source excerpts and tests cover timestamp disambiguation, ledger folding and watermarks, projection/cutoff behavior, pool promotion, scoped consolidator tools, worker launch/result IPC, memory paths/index rendering, status gauges, and timeline rendering.

The historical source contains internal documentation inconsistencies: PLAN describes chunkTokens 5000 and consolidate threshold 20000, while README says implementation complete and src/config defaults are 10000 and 15000; design snippets also vary on worker chunk delivery and whether the observer uses a shutdown terminal call.
